Open data from the publisher's portal

Source: R/src.R
ckanres.Rd

Police services, courts and corrections ministries publish through a few kinds of portal. These functions ask a portal where a dataset's files are now, and download one. ckanres() lists the files of a CKAN dataset and ckanls() searches a CKAN portal; socres() describes a Socrata dataset and gives the address of its CSV export; arcres() describes an ArcGIS feature layer and gives the address of a query for its rows; srcget() downloads an address to a file and returns its size and SHA-256, to be recorded with the analysis; scres() gives the address of a Statistics Canada table. srcls() lists sources the package knows by a short key (see Details), and srcurl() resolves one of them.

Usage

ckanres(portal, id)

ckanls(portal, q, rows = 50L)

socres(domain, id)

arcres(layer)

srcget(url, dest, over = FALSE, wait = 600)

srcls()

srcurl(key)

scres(pid, lang = c("en", "fr"))

Arguments

portal

The address of a CKAN portal, such as "https://data.ontario.ca".

id

A dataset's identifier on its portal: a CKAN package name or id, a Socrata four-by-four ("ijzp-q8t2").

q

Search words.

rows

The most datasets ckanls() returns, 1 to 1000.

domain

The host of a Socrata portal, such as "data.cityofchicago.org".

layer

The address of an ArcGIS feature layer, ending in its number (.../FeatureServer/0).

url

The address to download.

dest

The file to write.

over

TRUE replaces dest when it exists.

wait

The seconds to wait for the file (getOption("timeout") when that is longer).

key

A source's key, as srcls() lists it.

pid

The number of a Statistics Canada table: eight digits, with or without the hyphens of "35-10-0177-01" (the last two digits, the view, are not part of it).

lang

"en" (the default) or "fr": the language of the file.

Value

ckanres() a data frame with a row per file: name, format, url, modified and bytes (NA where the portal does not say). ckanls() a data frame with a row per dataset: id, title, files (their number) and licence. socres() and arcres() a list: name, url (the CSV export, or the GeoJSON query), columns (their names), updated (a POSIXct, or NA), and for a layer rows and max. srcget(), invisibly, a list: path, bytes, sha256 and url. scres() the address of the table's zipped CSV file. srcls() a data frame: key, publisher, what, kind ("ckan", "socrata", "arcgis", "statcan", "url" or "page"), portal and id. srcurl() one address: for a CKAN dataset the first CSV file's (else the first file's), for a page or a portal its own.

Details

Nothing is cached and nothing about a dataset is fixed in the package: a file the publisher has replaced is the one found. The files are the publisher's, under the licence the publisher states on its portal (ckanls() gives it for a CKAN dataset); read it before redistributing a file.

The sources of srcls(). In Canada: the Toronto Police Service's public safety data (ArcGIS layers: major crime indicators, homicides, shootings, neighbourhood crime rates, race-based data on use of force and on arrests and strip searches, Mental Health Act apprehensions), the City of Toronto's police annual statistical report and Montreal's criminal acts (CKAN), Ontario's data on people in custody (the Jahn settlement data), on use of force in correctional institutions and on people under correctional supervision (CKAN), Statistics Canada's tables of police-reported crime, the crime severity index, homicide, hate crime, adult criminal courts and correctional services, the director's reports of Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (one page each: ovrget()) and the Vancouver Police Department's crime data, which is behind a form that accepts its terms. In the United States: the police departments of New York City, Chicago and Los Angeles (Socrata), the Crime Data Explorer of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the National Crime Victimization Survey (pages). Elsewhere: the latest archive of the United Kingdom's street-level crime, outcomes and stop and search (over a gigabyte), Eurostat's police-recorded offences, and the open datasets of the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research (a page). The last rows are portals to search with ckanls(): Canada, Ontario, Toronto, Montreal, the United Kingdom and Australia. A source with no file of its own (a page, a portal) resolves to its address.

An ArcGIS layer returns at most max rows to one query (the layer's own limit, 1000 or 2000 as a rule): arcres() reports that limit and the layer's row count, and a larger layer is read in pages by adding &resultOffset= to the address.

Errors: a portal, domain, layer or url that is not one http:// or https:// address (a domain may be a bare host name); an id, q or key that is not one non-empty string; a pid that is not a table number; a portal that cannot be reached, does not answer in time or answers with an error; an answer that is not what that kind of portal sends; a dataset the portal does not have; a dest that is not one file path, or that exists without over = TRUE; a key srcls() does not list.

References

Wilkinson, M. D., Dumontier, M., Aalbersberg, I. J., Appleton, G., et al. (2016). The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship. Scientific Data, 3, 160018. doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.18

CKAN Association. CKAN API guide. https://docs.ckan.org/en/latest/api/

Tyler Technologies. Socrata Open Data API: API endpoints. https://dev.socrata.com/docs/endpoints

Esri. ArcGIS REST APIs. https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/

Statistics Canada. Web Data Service (WDS) user guide. https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/developers/wds/user-guide

Eurostat. Web services: access to the data by API (SDMX 2.1). https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/main/data/web-services

See also

odtab() for the tables the project's service mirrors and checks; ovrget() for one oversight report.

Examples

srcls()[, c("key", "publisher", "kind")]
#>                    key                                   publisher    kind

#> 8   toronto-asr-crimes                             City of Toronto    ckan

#> 11         siu-reports      Special Investigations Unit of Ontario    page
#> 12           vpd-crime                 Vancouver Police Department    page
#> 13        ontario-jahn   Ontario Ministry of the Solicitor General    ckan
#> 14         ontario-uof   Ontario Ministry of the Solicitor General    ckan
#> 15 ontario-supervision   Ontario Ministry of the Solicitor General    ckan
#> 16       statcan-crime                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 17         statcan-csi                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 18    statcan-homicide                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 19        statcan-hate                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 20      statcan-courts                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 21  statcan-admissions                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 22     statcan-custody                           Statistics Canada statcan
#> 23     nypd-complaints             New York City Police Department socrata
#> 24 nypd-complaints-ytd             New York City Police Department socrata
#> 25        nypd-arrests             New York City Police Department socrata
#> 26    nypd-arrests-ytd             New York City Police Department socrata
#> 27           nypd-hate             New York City Police Department socrata
#> 28          cpd-crimes                   Chicago Police Department socrata
#> 29         cpd-arrests                   Chicago Police Department socrata
#> 30         lapd-crimes               Los Angeles Police Department socrata
#> 31             fbi-cde             Federal Bureau of Investigation    page

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs the internet
f <- ckanres("https://data.ontario.ca",
             "jahn-settlement-data-inmates-ontario")
head(f[, c("name", "format", "modified")])
s <- socres("data.cityofchicago.org", "dpt3-jri9")
s$columns
g <- srcget(srcurl("tps-homicides"), tempfile(fileext = ".geojson"))
g$sha256
scres("35-10-0177-01")
} # }
try(srcurl("nowhere"))
#> Error : srcurl: `nowhere` is not a key of srcls().
